overview: Marazion’s beach is the one with the view everyone wants: St Michael’s Mount rising out of the bay just half a mile offshore. This is where the causeway to the island starts, so the beach is a natural part of any Mount day.
Marazion itself is a small, old market town on Mount’s Bay with a cluster of art galleries, cafés and an RSPB marsh reserve on its western edge, about two miles east of Penzance.

expect.title: The Mount
expect.text: At low tide a cobbled causeway runs from here to St Michael’s Mount; when the tide is in, little boats ferry people across.

expect.title: Marazion Marsh
expect.text: Just west of town is an RSPB reserve, good for a short, quiet walk and some birdwatching.

expect.title: Galleries and cafés
expect.text: The town has an active community of artists, with galleries selling paintings and pottery.

goodToKnow.label: Tides
goodToKnow.text: Check tide times if you plan to walk to the Mount: the causeway is only uncovered for a few hours around low water.

week.slot: Half a day with the Mount
week.text: Make this the starting point for a St Michael’s Mount day, timed around low tide. It faces south into Mount’s Bay, so it’s a good bet when the north coast is wild and windy.

pairWith.why: the island castle, reached by causeway or boat
a sandy village beach a little further east
art in a valley garden near Penzance

tips: Look up the tide times before anything else and plan your Mount crossing around them.
